concerns.text: FR-002 defines the asymptotic baseline Q_as(n) using Meinardus' theorem, but the theorem’s leading‑order term for distinct‑prime partitions is itself expressed in terms of prime‑density quantities (e.g., the pole of the prime zeta function, which is closely related to π(n) and 1/ln n). Because FR-004 later uses those same density quantities (π(n), 1/ln n, ∑_{p≤n}1/p) as predictors in the regression on the log‑residual R(n)=log p_P(n)−log Q_as(n), the validation target R(n) is not independent of the predictors. This creates a circular/tautological validation: any observed correlation may be forced by the way Q_as was constructed rather than reflecting a genuine systematic correction term.

FR-004 states that the density features must be derived “independently of the partition calculation,” yet it does not guarantee independence from the asymptotic baseline Q_as(n) defined in FR-002. Without an explicit statement that Q_as is computed without using those same density functions, the regression analysis cannot cleanly separate a true systematic bias from artefacts of the baseline definition.
